short: Founded Kyoto in 794 and pushed the frontier north, in the last reign of genuine imperial command.
full:
Kanmu took the throne in 781 and set out to free the court from the Nara monasteries and the entrenched families around them. In 784 he moved the capital to Nagaoka-kyō; after ten years of building, the assassination of the project's director and the death of his brother Prince Sawara in exile, the site was abandoned as ill-omened. In 794 he moved again, to Heian-kyō, laid out on a grid west of the Kamo river. It remained the imperial capital until 1869.

He also prosecuted the long war against the Emishi of the north-east, appointing Sakanoue no Tamuramaro as seii taishōgun — the title later shortened to shogun — who took Isawa in 802. Kanmu tightened provincial inspection, cut the conscript army, and sent the monks Saichō and Kūkai to China, whose Tendai and Shingon schools were established outside Nara's control. He died in 806. Within two generations the Fujiwara regents had taken over the government he had briefly held in his own hands.
